text:
RETAIL CONDUCT AUTHORITY FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Final rule: Overdraft fee transparency
Notice number: RCN-2026-001
Issued by: Retail Conduct Authority
Published: 2026-08-04
Effective date: 2027-02-01
1. Who this applies to
Banks and credit unions that offer deposit accounts with an overdraft service to consumers.
2. Background
Consumers told the Authority that overdraft fees often come as a surprise, because the fee is only visible on a statement days later. This rule makes the fee visible at the moment a consumer can still change course.
3. Requirements
3.1 Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, a firm must show the consumer the fee amount and give a choice to cancel the transaction.
3.2 A firm must send each consumer a monthly summary of all overdraft and returned-item fees charged in the previous month, with a year-to-date total.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-02-01.

obligations.text: Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, a firm must show the consumer the fee amount and give a choice to cancel the transaction.
obligations.controlDesc: App release test confirms the overdraft fee prompt and cancel option appear before a fee-bearing transaction
obligations.reason: Policy POL-FEE-01 states "Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, the app shows the fee and lets the customer cancel" and Control CTL-121 confirms "the overdraft fee prompt and cancel option appear before a fee-bearing transaction", which together satisfy the obligation's requirement to show the fee amount and give a choice to cancel before charging.

obligations.text: A firm must send each consumer a monthly summary of all overdraft and returned-item fees charged in the previous month, with a year-to-date total.
obligations.controlDesc: Monthly reconciliation that every account charged a fee received a fee summary with a year-to-date total
obligations.reason: Policy POL-FEE-01 provides a monthly statement of all fees charged with a year-to-date total, but does not specifically limit this to overdraft and returned-item fees as required by the obligation.
